newsitem.title: TURKEY: NO DEVALUATION, NO RATE INTERVENTION-TURK MINISTER.
newsitem.headline: NO DEVALUATION, NO RATE INTERVENTION-TURK MINISTER.

text.p: Gunes Taner, Turkey's state minister for the treasury, said the new coalition government would not go for a one-off devaluation nor intervene in the interest rate policy.
"In our practice, there will not be two things -- a devaluation and intervention in interest rates," Taner told Reuters.
Taner said the government would manage the economy through "fine tuning".

"By saying fine tuning, I mean that there won't be big interventions. To do this, the central bank has some instruments such as open market operations. We will run the economy by using these instruments," Taner said.
Turkey had last devalued its currency in early 1994.
The republic has led its lira fluctuate in line with supply and demand in the market under the central bank's tight grip since then.

Taner hinted that the government may not continue to auction two-year, inflation-indexed bonds -- an instrument heavily used by the former Islamist-led government to raise funds from the domestic market in the past four months.
"TUFEX (inflation-indexed bonds) is not a type of borrowing model I prefer," he said. He did not give any further details.
The inflation-index bonds make up 15 percent of the domestic debt stock which stood at 4,026.8 trillion lira at end-May.
